name: gate
wording: A point at a handover where the work stops for the operator's sign-off: a story's read-back, held by the architect; a story's plan read-back, held by the lead, which a task with no story skips unless the operator calls it; a pull request the operator reviews, held by the lead before it merges; release; a fork that is irreversible, about value or beyond the architect's competence; and any point the operator calls, stop included. A gate is an interrupt and nothing more: its holder, the party whose handover it is, ends its turn with a request for the operator's sign-off. Whoever receives that request holds no sign-off, so it brings it to the operator, and the holder goes on once it has the operator's answer. Pushing a branch or opening a pull request is never a gate, and between gates the agents work without checking in.
reason: The gate was built as machinery that detected, announced and shielded it. It needs none: a request for the operator's sign-off that ends its holder's turn reaches the operator by construction, since whoever receives it holds no sign-off and brings it on, and its passing through the delegating party on the way is no harm.
